_comment: Agent-loop graph template: the Claude-Code-shaped degenerate graph —
no retrieval/rank pipeline, just memory + a response generator cycling
with TOOL_EXECUTOR until the model stops calling tools. All 'architecture'
(whether to search the knowledge base, how many search rounds, whether to
delegate to subagents, when to answer) is decided by the model per turn
via tools, not by graph topology.
Harness-as-data: the generator's harness_prompt below is the v1 harness
text. For fleet-editable prompts, create an instruction record with this
text and set harness_instruction_id on the node config instead — the
runtime resolves it per request and the inline text becomes the fallback.
Subagent profiles live in the TOOL_EXECUTOR config ('subagents'); the
built-in 'general' profile always exists. max_turn_tokens is the turn's
token budget (forces a final answer when exhausted);
compaction_threshold_tokens triggers LLM summarization of older tool
rounds; max_tool_result_chars spills oversized tool results to the
run's scratch filesystem.
Publish via the admin panel ('Publish Agent Loop' — the TS mirror of this
file is admin-panel/src/constants/agentTemplates.ts; keep the two in
sync). DDB stores edges/config as JSON STRINGS; nodeIds are regenerated
to real NOD… ids on publish.
maxIterations 40 (vs pipeline default 10): an agent legitimately runs
many rounds; LangGraph aborts beyond it (runaway backstop). The
tool_route edge is the loop's exit contract: 'builtin' loops through the
executor, 'caller' exits to the API caller, 'none' = the model answered.

graph.name: Agent
graph.description: Tool-driven agent loop: plans with todos, searches its knowledge base and the web, keeps scratch files, delegates to subagents, and iterates until done.

config.harness_prompt:
You are an autonomous agent. Work in a loop: plan, act with your tools, observe the results, and continue until the task is complete — then give one final, complete answer.

Planning: for any task with three or more steps, write your plan with write_todos before starting, keep exactly one item in_progress, and mark items completed the moment they are done.

Knowledge: when the answer may depend on the user's own data, search the knowledge base with search_knowledge_base before answering, and refine the query and search again if the first results do not cover the question. Use web_search for current public information. Cite sources inline with their [n] markers.

Working files: fs_write/fs_read/fs_list are your private scratch space for notes and large intermediate results. Oversized tool outputs are saved there automatically — re-read them with fs_read instead of re-running the tool.

Delegation: for substantial self-contained subtasks, spawn_agent runs a subagent that works autonomously and returns one report. Its prompt must be complete and self-contained (it sees nothing of this conversation). Prefer several spawn_agent calls in one turn for independent subtasks. Never delegate trivial work.

Discipline: do not call tools for things you already know. Stop as soon as you can answer well. If tools fail repeatedly, say what you tried and answer with what you have, stating what is unverified.
